task_decomposition: Model 1 extracts the frozen evidence facts, including run counts, implemented variants, profiles, pass/fail totals, allowed claim categories, and forbidden claim categories.
Model 2 independently classifies claims C1-C6 as supported, unsupported, or forbidden using only the frozen evidence.

Model 3 reviews Model 2's classifications for overclaiming, numerical mismatch, and category mismatch, especially around production deployment, packet-capture benchmarking, public-chain benchmarking, media-plane QoE, and six-variant ablation claims.

Model 4 acts as final verifier/arbiter, compares all prior outputs against the frozen evidence, resolves disagreements conservatively, and emits the final evidence-bounded classification and rationale.
success_criteria: All classifications are grounded only in the frozen evidence.
Supported claims match explicit run counts, variant counts, or allowed claim categories.
Forbidden claims are rejected even if phrased similarly to allowed local-orchestration claims.
No production O-RAN, packet-capture network benchmark, public-chain, full media-plane QoE, or 240-run six-variant ablation validation is asserted.
The final verifier identifies C1, C2, and C5 as supportable, and C3, C4, and C6 as unsupported or forbidden.

The artifact includes a 240-run six-variant ablation study.
The results are a packet-capture network-impairment benchmark.
The evidence validates public-chain performance or full media-plane QoE.
The Stage D-real matrix includes more than the three implemented variants: full-l4, oracle-only, and no-ipfs.

Do not infer beyond local n8n artifact evidence.
